title.value: Improving Language Plasticity via Pretraining with Active Forgetting
title.justification: The title reflects the central concept of the paper, which focuses on enhancing language adaptability of pretrained language models using an active forgetting mechanism.
title.quote: Improving Language Plasticity via Pretraining with Active Forgetting

extractions.description: The paper discusses a novel method for improving the adaptability of pretrained language models (PLMs) to new languages by incorporating an active forgetting mechanism during pretraining. This technique involves periodically resetting the token embedding layer to encourage the model to re-learn, thus increasing its linguistic plasticity. The research shows that this method allows models to adapt faster and perform better in low-data regimes and for languages distant from English. It also reduces the computational cost of adapting PLMs to new languages.

sustainable_development_is_central.justification: The paper primarily focuses on improving language model adaptability to different languages by leveraging a novel forgetting technique. It does not address Climate or Ecological Sustainable Development directly.

primary_category.quote: Pretrained language models (PLMs) are today the primary model for natural language processing. Despite their impressive downstream performance, it can be difficult to apply PLMs to new languages, a barrier to making their capabilities universally accessible.

secondary_categories.quote: We propose to use an active forgetting mechanism during pretraining, as a simple way of creating PLMs that can quickly adapt to new languages.
